limitations: Capped run: the first 150 of 193 'test' images by sorted file name (max_images=150), to share CPU with a concurrently running stack.

Roboflow version preprocessing 'Stretch to 640x640' was applied by the dataset author before export, so the 'original' images evaluated here are the exported 640x640 images: camera frames of another aspect ratio are geometrically distorted (non-uniformly stretched) compared with what YOLOPv2 saw in training (BDD100K, 16:9).

Cross-dataset label convention: YOLOPv2's lane-line head was trained on BDD100K lane annotations (thin polylines along marking edges/centres, rendered at a fixed width), while this ground truth is hand-drawn polygons covering the painted marking. Line width, which markings are labelled (e.g. road edges, crosswalks, far-field dashes) and how dashed gaps are treated differ, so part of the measured error is convention mismatch, not model error. The exact pixel IoU of thin structures is very sensitive to 1-3 px offsets; read the tolerant numbers together with the exact ones.

Pixel-level metrics only: there is no per-lane instance matching (no TuSimple accuracy or CULane F1 with IoU-matched lanes), no lane type (solid/dashed) and no ego-lane assignment. YOLOPv2 outputs one binary lane-line mask and has no lane instances or types.
The service's fixed binary operating point (lane probability > 0.5) is evaluated; no threshold sweep.
Each exported image (already JPEG) is decoded and re-encoded once as JPEG q95 before inference, exactly as the video pipeline does, so results include one additional lossy compression step.

Production letterbox policy: the longest side is resized to 640 and the short side padded to a multiple of 32; the service crops the padding and resizes the lane probabilities back to the original H x W before thresholding.

The service ran the YOLOPv2 + RF-DETR-N ensemble; the lane mask is produced by YOLOPv2 alone, so model_sha256 is the YOLOPv2 checkpoint and the ensemble identity is recorded in details. Service latency includes both models.

protocol.input: exported image -> RGB -> JPEG q95 (app.video.encode.encode_jpeg_bytes, as the video pipeline) -> POST /v1/infer via app.perception.client.InferenceClient
protocol.prediction: lane_mask_png (YOLOPv2 lane-line probability > 0.5, unletterboxed to the original frame by the service) > 127
protocol.ground_truth: union of all annotation polygons of the image (all lane-marking classes), rasterised at the original resolution with cv2.fillPoly (vertices - 0.5 px, 4 fractional bits)
protocol.tolerance: k = max(1, floor(8 * W / 1280 + 0.5)) px; elliptical (disk) structuring element of size 2k+1; tolerant metrics dilate BOTH masks; buffered precision/recall dilate only the reference mask
protocol.dataset_level: sum of per-image counts over images, then ratios
protocol.per_image: ratios per image; undefined values (zero denominator) excluded and counted
